FGSM3 · Day 1 · Group Challenge

Build Your Online Consultation Clinic

You are launching a new primary-care service. Make choices, spend your budget, protect your patients, survive a crisis — then defend your clinic before the panel.

Your group task

Your goal is to design your online clinic.

Prepare a presentation and justify the choices your group makes throughout the simulation.

Everyone in your group should speak for approximately 2 minutes.

STEP 1 / 11

Open your clinic

You have 100 Clinic Credits. Your goal is to build a service that is safe, accessible, efficient and patient-friendly — then defend every major choice.

👥 3–4 students
One rule: do not look for a perfect answer. You are building a system for a population, with limited resources.

Keep it short. Your name will appear on your final clinic report.

STEP 4 / 11

Build your digital front door

How will patients contact you? Choose ONE access system. Remember: easy for the majority does not necessarily mean accessible for everyone.

💰 Spend wisely
Evidence drop: In England, GP practices must keep online consultation available throughout core hours, while patients can also contact the practice by phone or by walking in. Your design can be digital-led, but not digital-only. Open the NHS source ↗
STEP 5 / 11

Decide how requests are triaged

Every request has arrived. Who decides what happens next?

🩺 Clinical workflow

Patient alert: digital confidence ≠ clinical suitability

Robert requests a video consultation. Decide what your clinic should do next.

🚨 New request
● VIDEO REQUEST
ROBERT · 61

Persistent abdominal discomfort + unexplained weight loss

Usually healthy · confident internet user · asks for video because it is convenient.

STEP 7 / 11

Build the video consultation room

Place at least six objects in the room. You can drag them, or tap an object and then tap a room zone. Run the room test afterwards. Think about camera position, backlighting, sound, privacy and confidentiality.

🖱 Drag or tap

Desktop: drag objects. Touch/keyboard: select an object, then select a room zone. To remove an item, use the × button on the item in the room.

STEP 8 / 11

Spend your accessibility budget

You cannot buy everything. Choose the support that matters most for your population and your design.

♿ Inclusion
Evidence drop: NHS England’s digital inclusion framework highlights device/connectivity, accessibility, skills/capability, beliefs/trust, and partnerships. It also says digital services should complement non-digital support. Explore the framework ↗
STEP 9 / 11

Write your clinic rulebook

Select exactly SIX rules and discuss them before locking your policy. You will see the policy review only after you commit.

0 / 6 rules
Evidence drop: Current NHS England Digital guidance stresses privacy, permission if others are present, clear closure of the connection, and documentation of relevant outcomes. Open the 2026 guidance ↗
STEP 10 / 11

Here come the patients

Your earlier decisions now have consequences. Read the outcomes carefully: they will give you material for your final defence.

👥 System test
STEP 11 / 11

Something has gone wrong.

Every team receives one random crisis. You have one decision. Adapt your system, accept the trade-off, and remember what you did: the panel will ask.

⚠ Crisis mode
FINAL

Your clinic is ready for the panel

Do not simply describe what you built. Defend the compromises you made.

🎤 ~2 min per student

🎤 FINAL CHALLENGE · DEFEND YOUR CLINIC

Everyone must speak for approximately 2 minutes. For a group of 3–4, plan roughly 6–8 minutes in total. Use the clinic report below to justify your choices.

  1. Who does your clinic serve?
  2. What are your three most important decisions?
  3. What compromise did you make?
  4. How does your clinic protect vulnerable patients?
  5. How did you respond to the crisis?
  6. Why should the panel choose your clinic?
We chose … because …Compared with …, our system is …We prioritised … over …Although our system is more expensive, …The main drawback is …Patients who … are more likely to …Our solution is not perfect, but …
